name: Kajji real TUI startup across stress and real repositories

description: Baseline: fixed real TUI startup on stress and copied real repository

asi.hypothesis: Establish comparable fresh-process baseline before changes
asi.observations: Real fixture is stable at 3.37s; stress samples range 966–1282ms. Tests and typecheck pass.

description: Parse only new bookmark stream lines instead of reparsing the full prefix

asi.hypothesis: Incremental bookmark parsing reduces repeated allocations for large bookmark streams
asi.rollback_reason: Primary startup increased 24.6%; both workloads worsened. First-frame delay also increased, so environmental variation may contribute; no measured benefit.
asi.next_action_hint: Investigate startup import cost and subprocess critical path rather than parser micro-optimizations
asi.implementation: Maintain pending incomplete line plus immutable concatenated bookmark batches; retain final authoritative parse.

description: perf: overlap repository inspection with application module loading

asi.hypothesis: Start repository inspection before importing the full App component graph; await both before rendering
asi.observations: Primary improved 1.9%, but sample ranges are wide and first-frame median did not improve. This requires a repeat; no strong speed claim yet.
asi.validation: Unit tests and typecheck pass; rendering still waits for both modules and repository inspection.

description: Repeat the application-import overlap candidate without code changes

asi.hypothesis: Check whether the initial small improvement repeats
asi.observations: Repeat is faster, but unchanged code varied from 1827 to 1731ms. Need an A comparison before assigning the full improvement to code.
asi.next_action_hint: Test original static App import as A; retain fixed measurement and fixtures.

description: A comparison: restore static App import to test attribution

asi.hypothesis: Original static import may perform equally well once environmental variation is accounted for
asi.rollback_reason: Original static import is 1.54% slower than best candidate aggregate; restore candidate
asi.next_action_hint: Look for a larger deterministic reduction. Import overlap evidence is small, not a 7% proven gain.
asi.observations: A improved relative to first baseline too. Stress faster than candidate; real slower. Environmental drift accounts for much of initial apparent gain.

description: perf: reuse bounded ANSI parsing cache for bookmark stack rows

asi.hypothesis: Use the shared bounded parse cache instead of recreating a terminal parser for identical bookmark row text
asi.observations: Primary improved 1.05% from prior best; real workload worsened 4.6% while stress improved 6.4%. Small result needs repeat.
asi.validation: Tests and typecheck pass. Cache uses same cols=9999 and rows=1, resolves theme colors after retrieval, and is bounded by bytes and entries.

description: Retry incremental bookmark parsing after ANSI cache change and stream trace inspection

asi.hypothesis: Stable bookmark identities plus ANSI reuse may help the observed many-small-batch real workload
asi.rollback_reason: Again much worse startup, including first frame before bookmark parsing runs. No end-to-end improvement established.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not retry parser alone again. Investigate why edited source runs have higher first-frame import time and whether source transform caches skew A/B.
asi.observations: Both runs that edit large jj.ts have high first-frame costs. Same code file size 1200+ lines may have JSX preload transform cache invalidation effects; need inspect compiler cache or sustained repeat before attribution.

description: Memoize local bookmark filtering in sync and bookmark panel

asi.hypothesis: Avoid filtering all bookmark entries on each selected-bookmark read and panel count access
asi.rollback_reason: Primary worse than retained best; real samples 3477–4637ms are too variable to demonstrate benefit
asi.next_action_hint: Prioritize functional checks and source analysis while machine load is high; do not claim small timing changes as wins.
asi.environment: Observed load average ~12, with Sandbed, WindowServer, Figma and other Pi processes consuming CPU.

description: Remove unused ghostty-terminal registration and its startup import

asi.hypothesis: Unused renderer extension registration may load avoidable terminal-buffer code
asi.rollback_reason: Primary 5.2% slower than best; no measured startup benefit
asi.next_action_hint: Focus on large import modules or subprocess work; shared ghostty root already needed by ANSI parsing may load terminal code anyway
asi.validation: 20/21 E2E checks passed on retained code. File-navigation failure reproduces on base 996dbf68 in /tmp/kajji-startup-e2e-baseline. No tests weakened.

description: Use Shiki core imports for the explicit worker language and theme bundle

asi.hypothesis: Avoid importing the full language/theme registries when all supported grammars are passed directly
asi.rollback_reason: Primary startup 3.7% slower than best, without a clear highlighting benefit
asi.next_action_hint: Try Oniguruma engine to remove first-use regex compilation instead of small import changes. Verify language output and compiled worker.
asi.source: Inspected current /tmp/shiki bundle-factory: full factory delegates to core for explicit grammar/theme objects; semantic equivalence holds for this worker.

description: Use Shiki Oniguruma/WASM engine instead of JavaScript regex conversion

asi.hypothesis: Avoid expensive first-use grammar conversion/JIT while preserving TextMate highlighting
asi.rollback_reason: Primary content startup 12.8% worse than best despite faster syntax readiness
asi.next_action_hint: Keep as a separate highlighting optimization lead; primary metric here is content, not highlighting. Do not keep solely for secondary win.
asi.observations: Stress highlighting gap shrinks strongly; full factory uses supported inlined shiki/wasm loader. Tests pass but compiled binary still needs validation before retaining in a future session.

description: Memoize resolved theme colors to avoid repeated color calculations and object allocations

asi.hypothesis: Shared memo avoids rebuilding adapted theme colors for every mounted row and span
asi.rollback_reason: No primary improvement; startup 13% above best
asi.next_action_hint: Small allocation savings are insufficient for startup target. Inspect substantial pre-render initialization or command duplication instead.
asi.validation: All unit tests and typecheck pass; colors still react to theme, mode and terminal background.

description: Avoid JSX compilation of sync provider through equivalent createComponent call and .ts module

asi.hypothesis: Native TypeScript loading avoids Babel transform of 1400-line file with only one JSX expression
asi.rollback_reason: Primary 3.7% slower than best. No sufficient gain to justify rename and explicit component construction.
asi.next_action_hint: Stop small source-only changes. Inspect actual jj bookmark command cost or larger import graph deferral with correctness safeguards.
asi.validation: Same provider value and getter children; unit tests and types pass. Benchmark/readiness code unchanged.

description: perf: share bookmark target descriptions across pinned reference reads

asi.hypothesis: Evaluate expensive target empty/description formatting once per unique commit rather than once per local and remote reference
asi.observations: Real startup falls to 1841ms from prior 3184ms; primary improves 20.8% vs prior best, despite slower first frame. Stress remains about 1s.
asi.correctness: Compared full Bookmark arrays against original template for both fixtures, with default and custom scoped colors/ID aliases: exact equality. Original fallback retained for conflicted/deleted refs and unpinned reads. Tests and types pass.
asi.implementation: Reference read preserves per-reference ID aliases. Metadata reads use bookmark list (not log) to preserve label scopes; choose representative ref per target, group by remote, bound names/argv, concurrency 2. Currently publishes final Complete only on shared path; add progressive batches plus regression tests next.
asi.scope: User explicitly approved larger shared metadata read change via question.
asi.tool_issue: Discard of renamed sync module left a zero-byte untracked sync.ts shadowing sync.tsx. Removed that tool artifact before this run.

description: perf: stream shared bookmark descriptions in bounded concurrent groups

asi.hypothesis: Publish fully hydrated reference prefixes as metadata arrives while evaluating each target once
asi.observations: Primary improves another 2.3%; real median1794ms. Progressive display restored without marking Complete before all metadata streams finish.
asi.validation: 11 new tests cover shared targets, argument bounds, out-of-order groups, immutable snapshots, errors, cancellation of both active child streams, native remote/divergent/deleted/conflicted refs, custom colors and ID aliases. All unit tests and types pass.
asi.correctness: Only full128-hex operation IDs use multi-read optimization; symbolic/unpinned operations retain original single-read path. Metadata remains in bookmark_list scope and reference ID formatting stays per reference.
asi.formatting: Fixed previously retained tui.tsx Promise.all formatting.

description: Serialize hydrated-prefix publication after merging concurrent metadata sources

asi.hypothesis: Joining after the concurrent stream merge gives an explicit monotonic publication guarantee and avoids shared producer-side state
asi.rollback_reason: Measured primary worse than best amid high variation; save correctness hardening for next candidate rather than claiming a speed win
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply .auto/publication-order.patch with next shared-read optimization. This is a correctness hardening requirement, not an optional speed tweak. Try fewer metadata subprocess setup costs or bounded concurrency4.
asi.validation: 17 tests pass including native default/all-remotes, errors, symbolic operations, missing metadata fallback, cancellation. Native test now checks monotonic prefix lengths.
asi.risk: Producer-side accumulator in retained version constructs snapshots before merged delivery; ordering should be made explicit even though native tests pass.

description: perf: read up to four independent bookmark target groups concurrently

asi.hypothesis: Use bounded concurrency4 to overlap independent pinned metadata groups while keeping prefix joins downstream of the merge
asi.observations: Real startup improves to1417ms, primary1214ms. Stress1039ms roughly baseline; one slow stress sample1517ms confirms remaining environmental variation.
asi.validation: 17 regression tests plus full unit suite and types pass. Includes prior publication-order hardening and symbolic-operation safeguards.
asi.correctness: No producer-side shared accumulator; prefixes are constructed only after merged delivery, so publication cannot reorder snapshots.
asi.next_action_hint: Verify A/B/A with shared path disabled temporarily, plus third small fixture and E2E. Do not tune concurrency solely against one large fixture.

description: Original-source A comparison interrupted before completion

asi.hypothesis: Verify retained startup improvement against original source in a separate workspace
asi.rollback_reason: User interrupted the run; no valid measurement was produced
asi.next_action_hint: User now requests one bundled-binary startup run. Pause optimization loop and measure the installed executable separately without comparing it as a like-for-like source result.

name: Single release-settings bundled Kajji startup on copied real repository

description: Single release-settings bundled-binary startup measurement on copied real repository

asi.hypothesis: Measure actual compiled startup separately from source launches, as requested
asi.scope: Exactly one measured bundled launch, no warmup. Built current code with same minify, conditions, worker entrypoint and compile flags as scripts/build.ts. Installed binary not replaced.
asi.observations: Content and highlighting ready2015.6ms; first visible1293.9ms. This one sample is not a stable comparison with source medians. First bundled launch may include OS binary validation and cold executable pages.
asi.readiness: Same frame observer, content readiness conditions, fixture copy policy, terminal dimensions and navigation validation. Local adapter changes only launch argv and module import paths.
asi.next_action_hint: User requested a single run and pause. Do not resume optimization loop without a new request. Use compiled baseline for future optimization if requested.

description: Verify bundled startup with a second launch of the unchanged executable

asi.hypothesis: The first newly compiled binary launch includes extra executable loading or OS validation costs that may not recur
asi.observations: Identical SHA256 executable: content startup dropped2015.6→897.1ms, first frame1259.9→227.2ms. Most of the difference occurs before the first frame. This is measurement verification, NOT a code optimization.
asi.uncertainty: Cannot isolate OS validation, executable page caching, and reduced machine load from two samples. Load average decreased from prior high contention. Do not claim a55.5% code improvement.
asi.validation: Same copied fixture,2898 references,100 revisions,frame readiness and navigation checks; all unit tests and typechecks pass.
asi.next_action_hint: Future compiled comparisons need equal first-launch/warmup policy and repeated processes across both real and stress fixtures. Rebuild after every source change; never measure a stale binary.

name: Compiled Kajji startup with equal warmup across stress and real repositories

description: Baseline compiled startup with one warmup and three measured processes per workload

asi.hypothesis: Equal warmup and repeated compiled launches provide a fairer optimization baseline than first launches or source runs
asi.validation: Rebuilt current source with release settings; one excluded warmup per fixture; three measured fresh processes each. Fixtures and readiness conditions unchanged. Full tests and typecheck pass.
asi.observations: Real content median780.8ms; stress263.2ms. Combined453.3ms is geometric mean, not a directly observed launch. Average per-fixture first-visible median187.4ms. No source code change or claimed optimization.
asi.next_action_hint: Now test Oniguruma on compiled workload; source discard was on a different target. Preserve all languages, themes, fallback and correctness checks. Do not compare new segment numerically with source or single-launch segments.

description: perf: use Oniguruma for bundled syntax highlighting

asi.hypothesis: Oniguruma avoids first-use JavaScript regex compilation and reduces startup CPU contention in the compiled executable
asi.observations: New compiled target and equal warmup policy: primary improves4.9%; real781→699ms, stress263→266ms. Highlighted median average876→526ms. Peak sampled RSS275→347MiB (+26%) is a tradeoff, not catastrophic.
asi.validation: Compiled release with inlined WASM loads successfully, all measured launches reach syntax readiness and navigate correctly. Full unit tests and types pass. No language/theme/fallback/readiness changes.
asi.next_action_hint: Expand multilingual worker tests and repeat against JavaScript engine under same compiled workload before attributing small primary win. Investigate RSS increase; do not claim same colors for every grammar without checking.

description: Test Shiki core imports with multilingual worker regression coverage

asi.hypothesis: Core-only Shiki imports might avoid full registry initialization in the compiled worker
asi.rollback_reason: New test samples inferred as string[][] rather than tuples, causing typecheck failure. Benchmark also worse than retained431ms and memory unchanged/worse.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not retry core alone. Restore .auto/multilingual-tests.patch and type samples as [string,string][]; verify retained full-factory Oniguruma behavior and memory before new changes.
asi.validation: Runtime multilingual test passed all30 languages and both themes243 assertions, but static typecheck correctly rejected the test. Full suite stopped before execution.

description: test: cover all bundled syntax languages and verify Oniguruma startup again

asi.hypothesis: Retained Oniguruma should repeat its compiled startup benefit and preserve colored text in all configured languages
asi.validation: Thirty languages times two themes preserve complete source text and produce multiple token colors. Includes Unicode, long-line and unknown-language fallbacks. Corrected tuple typing; all unit tests and typecheck pass.
asi.observations: Primary428.1ms vs prior431.2ms; real714.6ms vs698.6ms. Repeat close enough to support stability but not an additional code speed claim. Memory346MiB confirms tradeoff persists.
asi.next_action_hint: A/B/A JavaScript engine control with same rebuilt compiled protocol. Expanded test may expose preexisting JS grammar fallback; do not weaken it.

description: A comparison: restore JavaScript regex engine under the same compiled workload

asi.hypothesis: Check whether the apparent Oniguruma startup gain survives an original-engine A comparison
asi.rollback_reason: JavaScript primary438.1ms is2.3% worse than retained428.1ms; restore Oniguruma. Both engines pass all multilingual checks.
asi.observations: Real startup707ms is nearly equal to Oniguruma715ms, unlike first baseline781ms. Most original10% real gain was environmental. Highlighting834.96ms vs531.92ms remains a clear difference. Memory276.55MiB vs346.31MiB confirms about70MiB cost.
asi.next_action_hint: Report primary benefit as small/inconclusive, highlighting improvement as strong. Seek reduced Oniguruma memory or unrelated startup bottleneck; do not claim6% proven primary gain.

description: Wait for the initial log stream before viewport prefetch requests an expanded page

asi.hypothesis: Avoid canceling useful initial-page work when prefetch sees a partially streamed log
asi.rollback_reason: Primary startup33% above best; sequentially completing initial and expanded pages did not improve end-to-end timing. First frame also slower, so environmental load may contribute.
asi.next_action_hint: If revisited, investigate viewport prefetch demand itself and response to user navigation, not this sequential wait alone. Do not reduce initial data or change readiness just to improve metric.
asi.validation: Regression test proved initial51-record stream completes without cancellation, two concurrent expansion requests coalesce into one101-record request, final100 commits preserved. Tests and typecheck passed.
asi.implementation: logStreamHandle typed as ReturnType<typeof app.jjStreamLogPage>; await its result and recheck token/hasMore/loadingMore before expansion.

description: Start PR metadata reads once bookmark streaming completes instead of per partial batch

asi.hypothesis: Avoid repeated git-origin resolution, GraphQL query construction and canceled gh processes during bookmark streaming
asi.rollback_reason: Primary550ms is28.5% above best; no measured startup improvement. Environment slower before first frame too, but cannot claim a gain.

asi.hypothesis: Build-time bytecode compilation moves JavaScript parsing out of process startup
asi.rollback_reason: Bun1.4.2 rejected top-level await in index.tsx with bytecode enabled under implicit output format. Build failed before any benchmark launch.
asi.next_action_hint: Explicit ESM output may be required. Check installed runtime behavior; current upstream docs support ESM+compile but may be newer. Do not drop async startup/error handling to force a build.
